headline: Clorox drops as ERP lap and GOJO step-up compress margins
summary_short: Clorox Q4 FY2026 net sales fell 2% to $1.95B (organic -13%) as the year-ago ERP transition shipments lap distorted the comparison. GOJO acquisition (closed April) added 10 points to reported sales. Adjusted EPS dropped 42% to $1.66.
summary_long: Reported net sales of $1.95B included ~10 points from the GOJO/Purell acquisition. Organic sales fell 13%, with ~13.5 points attributable to lapping incremental ERP-transition shipments in Q4 FY2025. Gross margin compressed 520 bps to 41.3% on lower volume, GOJO inventory step-up (~150 bps), commodity costs, and manufacturing/logistics costs, partially offset by cost savings. GAAP EPS $1.34 (-50% y/y) included GOJO transaction/integration costs. Adjusted EPS $1.66 (-42%). Segment picture: Health & Wellness sales +16% (GOJO boost) but adjusted EBIT -15%; Household -18% sales, -56% EBIT; Lifestyle -17% sales, -60% EBIT; International +4% sales on FX. FY2026 total net sales $6.72B (-5%). Management characterized results as in-line with expectations and framed FY2027 outlook as continuing challenging with cost volatility and value-seeking consumers.

drivers.explanation: Lapping the ~13.5 percentage points of incremental ERP-transition shipments in the year-ago quarter; GOJO acquisition added about 10 points offset.
Lower volume, GOJO inventory step-up (~150 bps), higher commodity costs, and higher manufacturing and logistics costs, partially offset by cost savings.
Lower net sales and gross margin combined with GOJO transaction-related costs including inventory step-up and integration costs, partially offset by lapping prior-year digital investments.

confidence_notes: Filing-based summary from Exhibit 99.1 press release accompanying the August 3 2026 8-K. Clorox uses a June fiscal year; this is Q4 FY2026 (Apr-Jun 2026) — our shard labels it FY2026 Q2 which follows Yahoo's calendar-Q convention. All figures y/y vs Q4 FY2025 as company disclosed. Organic sales, adjusted EPS, and adjusted EBIT are non-GAAP measures.
